parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift:39) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift:43) are interfaces in the same `Core` package sharing 3 of 3 members: `name: Notification.Name`, `makeNotification(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification`, and a `makeMessage` factory. The sole structural difference is that `MainActorNotificationMessage.makeMessage` marks its `Notification` parameter as `sending` (for actor-isolation transfer), while `AsyncNotificationMessage` does not. Introducing a base PAT `NotificationMessage` with the shared `name` property and `makeNotification` requirement, then having each existing protocol refine it and add only its own `makeMessage` variant, eliminates the duplicated surface while preserving the concurrency-semantic distinction. Both protocols already use `Self` as the return type of `makeMessage`, confirming they are already written in a PAT-friendly style.
